status: draft-only: recall/dedupe and memory persistence unverified

cards.title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation
cards.mechanism: Attach an explicit evidence-link field (source episode/session/utterance ID) to every triplet edge at write time in the graph store, and expose it in triplet_query_as_of/triplet_supersede results so retrieval and contradiction-resolution can rank/filter by evidence traceability and recency, not just edge existence.

expected_gain.metric: nDCG@20 on chitta golden recall set
expected_gain.rationale: chitta already has temporal triplet versioning (triplet_query_as_of/triplet_supersede) and memory-level provenance (memory_provenance, provenance_check), but no per-edge evidence link inside the triplet/graph store itself — this closes that specific gap the survey flags as core to graph representation.

cost.blast_radius: chitta-field/src/store.rs triplet schema, chitta/include/chitta/rpc/field_handler.hpp, field_memory_recall.cpp ranking path

evidence.claim: Abstract states graph-based personalized memory models user info "through explicit relations, temporal context, and evidence links"
Abstract frames memory evolution (revision) and retrieval as lifecycle stages built on those representations

cards.title: When Users Don't Ask: Benchmarking Context-Driven Memory Retrieval in Conversational Agents
cards.mechanism: Add a query-rewriting/expansion pre-pass to recall that converts implicit and composed conversational queries (context-derived, not explicit asks) into explicit multi-facet sub-queries before hitting the RRF lanes, targeting the paper's finding that implicit/composed queries have the largest retrieval gap and that rewriting narrows it for raw-turn memory

expected_gain.metric: nDCG@20 on implicit/composed query subset (golden-set style eval)
expected_gain.rationale: chitta's hybrid/RRF recall (handle_recall_gateway, strategy=hybrid) and cross-encoder rerank already improve explicit/keyword recall, but nothing rewrites implicit context-only queries into explicit sub-queries, which is exactly the gap this paper measures

cost.blast_radius: chitta-mcp/server.py handle_recall_gateway/handle_recall_smart, prompt-hook.sh query construction, adds one LLM call per recall on implicit-query heuristic

evidence.claim: Paper finds conversational framing exposes retrieval gaps on implicit and composed queries beyond QA benchmarks
Multi-facet query rewriting narrows the gap for raw-turn memory but not abstractive memory

cards.title: AgenticRag-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Stack Memory for Multi-Step Reasoning, Retrieval and Memorizing
cards.mechanism: Add a stack-based memory scratchpad to recall_smart/recall_gateway: instead of one-shot RRF merge, let the agent push/pop retrieval sub-goals so intermediate retrieved facts persist across multi-hop steps and get scored by an action-aware reward (retrieve/verify/memorize as distinct fine-grained actions) rather than only a trajectory-level RRF merge

expected_gain.rationale: chitta already does multi-lane RRF hybrid recall (78.0% on longmemeval_s) but has no explicit multi-hop stack/scratchpad or per-action reward shaping, so gains would come from better long-horizon retrieval chaining, not from adding memory itself

cost.blast_radius: chitta-mcp/server.py recall_gateway/recall_smart handlers, field_memory_recall.cpp RRF merge path, no daemon storage schema change expected

evidence.claim: Paper reports stack memory + fine-grained action space + hierarchical action-aware rewards improve multi-hop reasoning/retrieval over trajectory-level-reward baselines
Abstract states existing agentic RAG RL methods use coarse action spaces and trajectory-level rewards causing weak reward assignment
